chose: A core dependency is a visible component called by more than half of the other visible components, by at least three, with at least three quarters of its component interfaces incoming; drawn as a rail at the foot with a stub under each caller
over: called by more than half alone
because: on Mnemion both Core and Hive are called by all seven others, but Hive calls five components and is the domain hub, not a utility; the in-share clause keeps Hive a station and makes Core the rail. On Coherence the rule yields Adapters, Journal and Spec, and leaves Enforcement (called by 7 of 9, calls 4) a station. Every term is the component's own counts plus the visible count, so the rule cannot move a component an added interface does not touch

chose: A component's column is its distance from where work enters capped at two and read from its own callers (0 declares an entrance, or is the root when none is declared, or nothing calls it; 1 an entrance's component calls it; 2 otherwise); its row is its folder order among visible components, one row each
over: columns by true distance from the entrances
rows chosen to straighten each route
because: the stability rule (adding one interface moves only the components it touches) and true distance conflict: an added interface shortens the distance of components downstream of its callee, so they would move. The order says keep stability and record the trade: distance is exact on both Mnemion (max 2) and Coherence (max 1), rows follow folders, and routes are straightened by octilinear routing and port ordering instead of by placement

chose: A structural route is the declaring component, the handler's component, then from each stop the heaviest component interface (most reference sites, ties by folder) to a component not yet on it and not a core dependency; entrances whose routes are the same stops share one line; with no entrance declared, one route per root interface
over: the whole reachable set of an entrance lit as its route
because: a transit line is a path, not a reach set; the heaviest interface is the evidence-backed guess at where work goes next from a component, since interfaces carry no per-entrance attribution. Sharing a line between entrances with identical stops is one route drawn once, not a merged bundle of different routes. Mnemion declares no entrances, so its four routes are derived from the root's interfaces and the canvas says so
